title: Polynomial algebra of bi-invariant differential operators
notes: For a real semisimple group the notes identify the bi-invariant differential operators with a polynomial ring in \(\ell\) generators, where \(\ell\) is the rank; for \(SL(n)\), there is one generator in each degree \(2,\ldots,n\). Gelfand calls all these generators ``Laplace operators.
statement: For a connected real semisimple Lie group \(G\), the algebra of complex-valued differential operators invariant under left and right translations is \(Z(U(\mathfrak g_{\mathbb C}))\). The Harish-Chandra isomorphism identifies it with \(S(\mathfrak h_{\mathbb C})^W\), hence with a polynomial algebra on \(\operatorname{rank}_{\mathbb C}\mathfrak g_{\mathbb C}\) generators. For \(\mathfrak{sl}_n\), their orders are \(2,\ldots,n\).
reconstruction: Connectedness and complex coefficients are supplied. ``Rank'' is complex absolute rank, not real split rank. The historical name ``Laplace operator'' here includes higher-order central operators.
fate: The central-operator construction predates the lecture; see \citet[pp.~103--104]{gelfand1950center}.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026, this remains an established construction under the stated hypotheses.

title: Gelfand’s cyclic trace generators
notes: Gelfand writes \(E_{ij}f(x)=\frac d{dt}|_0f(x(1+te_{ij}))\), then \(\sum E_{ii}\), \(\sum E_{ik}E_{ki}\), and \(\sum E_{ij}E_{jk}E_{ki}\). He says subsequent expressions depend on the first \(n\) and refers to ``Gelfand, 1947.
statement: In \(U(\mathfrak{gl}_n(\mathbb C))\), set \(c_r=\sum_{i_1,\ldots,i_r}E_{i_1i_2}\cdots E_{i_ri_1}\). These central elements, for \(1\le r\le n\), generate the center. Passing to \(\mathfrak{sl}_n\) removes \(c_1\), leaving generators of degrees \(2,\ldots,n\).
reconstruction: The path \(1+te_{ii}\) is taken in \(GL_n\); the trace-free restriction gives the \(SL_n\) statement. Noncommuting factors are retained in their written cyclic order. The bibliographic date is not silently corrected to a first-circulation date.
fate: The matching paper appeared in 1950, received 3 July 1948: \citet[\S2, example~1, pp.~105--106; \S3, Theorem~2, p.~108]{gelfand1950center}.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026, the construction is classical. The notebook's 1947 reference remains a provenance discrepancy; earlier circulation has not been established.
speaker: I. M. Gelfand

title: Centrally finite invariant distributions
notes: The notes impose \(T^x=T\) and \(JT=0\), where \(R=\mathbb C[D_1,\ldots,D_\ell]\) and \(\dim R/J<\infty\); maximal ideals give ordinary joint eigenvalues, whereas \((D-\lambda)^2T=0\) illustrates a generalized eigencondition.
statement: A distribution \(T\in\mathcal D'(G)\) is invariant and centrally finite if it is conjugation invariant and some finite-codimensional ideal \(J\subset Z(U(\mathfrak g_{\mathbb C}))\) annihilates it. For a maximal ideal \((D_i-\lambda_i)_i\), this is the joint eigendistribution condition. Finite codimension permits finite generalized joint eigenspaces; it does not require a maximal ideal.
fate: This is the finite-ideal framework of \citet[\S2, Lemma~1]{harishchandra1965algebra}; see also \citet[Definition~1.6.1]{galinalaurent2003characters}.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026, this remains an established construction under the stated hypotheses.

title: Local integrability and regular-set analyticity
notes: Kirillov's main theorem says that a conjugation-invariant distribution annihilated by a finite-codimensional central ideal is locally summable; it is analytic at regular points but need not be continuous everywhere.
statement: For a connected real reductive group in Harish-Chandra's setting, an invariant, centrally finite distribution on an invariant open set is represented by a locally integrable function. Its restriction to the regular semisimple set is real analytic. In particular, this applies to invariant eigendistributions and to distribution characters in the admissible irreducible setting. Analyticity is not asserted across the singular set.
reconstruction: The open set, the reductive setting, and ``regular semisimple'' are made explicit. The theorem is local; no assertion that all such distributions are characters, nor any classification of all unitary representations, follows.
fate: Already announced in 1963 and proved by 1965; \citet[Introduction; \S1.6]{galinalaurent2003characters} reviews the group theorem.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026, this is Harish-Chandra regularity, not an open problem. A later algebraic proof is given in \citet[Theorem~1.6.2, Corollary~1.6.3]{galinalaurent2003characters}.

title: Unidentified normalization of characters at infinity
notes: The sentence reads \ru{Характеры обращ. в 1 в $\infty$ --- м.б. разрывы}: characters become \(1\) at infinity and may have discontinuities. The scan supports the numeral \(1\) and the infinity sign.
statement: No precise assertion can be recovered: neither a character class, a normalization, nor the meaning of the limiting regime is specified.
reconstruction: This is not replaced by a decay theorem or by the normalization of a spherical function at the identity.
fate: Neither the group regularity theorem nor its modern restatement identifies this sentence; compare \citet[\S1.6]{galinalaurent2003characters}.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026, the intended normalization remains unidentified. There is no well-posed problem to develop.

title: Regular transverse sections and elliptic regularity
notes: The notes stratify conjugacy classes, choose a transverse \(\ell\)-dimensional section, assert that the radial operators have finite codimension in all differential operators, and write \(\Delta=\sum D_i^2\). After obtaining a polynomial in \(\Delta\) in \(J\), they conclude \(\Delta T=0\).
statement: Near a regular semisimple element, conjugation invariance reduces the distribution to a Cartan slice. Its radial joint equations form an analytic elliptic system. Finite central codimension supplies polynomial annihilators for the generators. Combining equal-order powers of these annihilators with their formal adjoints gives an elliptic scalar consequence. The radial invariant polynomial algebra is a finite invariant subalgebra in the appropriate Cartan polynomial ring; it is not of finite vector-space codimension in the full algebra of differential operators.
reconstruction: The construction of an elliptic consequence repairs the sketch. With generators of unequal orders, the displayed sum of squares need not be elliptic in the ordinary single-order sense. The immediate conclusion from \(P(\Delta)\in J\) is \(P(\Delta)T=0\), not \(\Delta T=0\), unless the latter symbol has been renamed.
fate: The analytic regular-set step is in \citet[\S2, Lemma~1]{harishchandra1965algebra}.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026, the intended elliptic-system argument is established; the literal finite-codimension and scalar-operator shortcuts require emendation.

title: Induction through semisimple centralizers and the Lie algebra
notes: The proof is divided into semisimple, ``nilpotent,'' and identity cases. A noncentral semisimple point descends to its smaller reductive centralizer; logarithm and exponential are used near the identity; the nilpotent case requires another argument.
statement: Harish-Chandra descent reduces the local problem at a noncentral semisimple element to its reductive centralizer, of smaller semisimple dimension. Central elements are translated to the identity. A local analytic exponential comparison reduces the remaining group problem to the Lie algebra, where nilpotent orbits require a separate argument. In a linear algebraic group the group counterpart of a nilpotent Lie-algebra element is unipotent.
reconstruction: The comparison near the identity includes analytic density/conjugation factors and is not the bare substitution \(X\mapsto\exp X\) for every central differential operator. The three cases are a proof plan, not a disjoint exhaustive Jordan decomposition as literally listed.
fate: The 1965 proof explicitly uses centralizers and nilpotent analysis: \citet[Introduction]{harishchandra1965algebra}.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026, this remains an established construction under the stated hypotheses.

title: The conjugation map is a submersion on the descent domain
notes: For semisimple \(a\), the notes put \(\mathfrak z=\mathfrak g^a\), let \(\Xi\) be its connected subgroup, and define \(\varphi(x,y)=xayx^{-1}\), \(V_a(y)=\det(\operatorname{Ad}((ay)^{-1})-1)_{\mathfrak g/\mathfrak z}\), and \(\Xi'=\{V_a\ne0\}\). ``Theorem 1 (Lemma 14)'' says \(\operatorname{rank}d\varphi=\dim G\).
statement: Let \(a\) be semisimple, \(\Xi=Z_G(a)^0\), and \(\Xi'\) the indicated open subset. Then \(\varphi:G\times\Xi'\to G\) is a smooth analytic submersion. In tangent coordinates at \((1,y)\), obtained by right multiplication \(y\exp(tZ)\) and left trivialization at \(ay\), \[d\varphi(X,Z)=(\operatorname{Ad}((ay)^{-1})-1)X+Z.\] Invertibility on \(\mathfrak g/\mathfrak z\) and the \(Z\)-term prove surjectivity.
reconstruction: The determinant is a function, not an assertion of nonvanishing for every \(y\in\Xi\); it is nonzero at \(y=1\), so the useful neighborhood is nonempty. This is a submersion, not a globally unique representative of each conjugacy class.
fate: This belongs to the 1965 group descent proof, \citet[pp.~457--508]{harishchandra1965group}; the notebook's Lemma~14 number was not independently verified.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026, this remains an established construction under the stated hypotheses.

title: Fiber integration and distributional pullback under a submersion
notes: For a submersion \(\pi:M\to N\) and smooth volume measures, \(\alpha\in C_c^\infty(M)\) is sent to \(f_\alpha\in C_c^\infty(N)\) by \(\int_M\alpha(F\circ\pi)d\mu=\int_NFf_\alpha d\nu\). The verbal phrase says generalized functions move ``from \(M\) to \(N\).'' The next lecture corrects the direction in a diagram.
statement: With positive smooth densities fixed, fiber integration defines a continuous map \(\pi_!:C_c^\infty(M)\to C_c^\infty(N)\). Its transpose defines the pullback \(\pi^*:\mathcal D'(N)\to\mathcal D'(M)\), with \(\langle\pi^*T,\alpha\rangle=\langle T,\pi_!\alpha\rangle\). No properness is needed for compactly supported test functions; pushing arbitrary distributions forward would require an additional support/properness condition.
reconstruction: The map is phrased in densities to avoid orientation assumptions. The verbal direction of transfer is separated from the displayed, correct test-function formula.
fate: A standard distributional ingredient of the descent reviewed in \citet[Introduction; \S1.6]{galinalaurent2003characters}; the notebook itself gives its local product proof.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026, this remains an established construction under the stated hypotheses.

title: Mixed differential notation for conjugation
notes: Kirillov writes \(f(x;D_1:y;D_2)\) for differentiation in both variables and uses \(f(x:y)=f(xyx^{-1})\), omitting identity operators.
statement: For a smooth function \(f\) on \(G\), put \(F(x,y)=f(xyx^{-1})\). Then \(f(x;D_1:y;D_2)=(D_{1,x}D_{2,y}F)(x,y)\), with the order and left/right invariant conventions fixed consistently. This notation introduces the bilinear operator \(\Gamma_y\) in record 121.
fate: Expository notation for the group proof cited as \citet{harishchandra1965group}; no independent theorem is asserted.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026, this remains an established construction under the stated hypotheses.

title: Pseudodifferential operators between vector bundles
notes: For compact smooth \(X\) and bundles \(E_1,E_2\), locally cut off operators \(\psi_iA\varphi_i\) must be ordinary matrix pseudodifferential operators; if \(\varphi\psi=0\), \(\psi A\varphi\) is smoothing.
statement: For smooth finite-rank complex bundles on a closed smooth manifold, a continuous linear map on smooth sections is a pseudodifferential operator of order \(m\) if its localized expressions lie in the prescribed coordinate symbol class and its Schwartz kernel is smooth off the diagonal. Cutoffs with disjoint supports give smoothing compositions. The stated pointwise condition \(\varphi\psi=0\) also suffices for finite-order pseudodifferential kernels: the product \(\psi(x)\varphi(y)\) is flat along the diagonal where the supports touch.
reconstruction: The symbol class, order, and continuity are supplied. Pointwise zero product is not erroneously replaced by a supposedly necessary positive separation of supports.
fate: Dynin's prelecture exposition gives this localization: \citet[\S1.2]{dynin1966index}, submitted March 1965, published 1966.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026, this remains an established construction under the stated hypotheses.

title: The Hodge–de Rham operator and its square
notes: The notes use all inhomogeneous differential forms, set \(\delta=d^*\), call \(d+\delta\) a Cauchy--Riemann operator, and identify \((d+\delta)^2\) with the Laplacian.
statement: On a closed Riemannian manifold \(X\), \(D=d+d^*\) acts on \(\Omega^*(X;\mathbb C)\), exchanges even and odd forms, and satisfies \(D^2=dd^*+d^*d=\Delta\), the Hodge Laplacian, which preserves form degree. The bundles are \(\Lambda^*T^*X\otimes\mathbb C\); a metric can identify tangent and cotangent bundles.
reconstruction: The modern name is the Hodge--de Rham Dirac operator. The notebook's use of \(\Lambda TX\) is interpreted via the metric rather than as the natural bundle of differential forms.
fate: Already in \citet[\S1.3, example~7]{dynin1966index}.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026, this remains an established construction under the stated hypotheses.

title: Harmonic representatives for de Rham cohomology
notes: Hodge's theorem is written \(\ker\Delta|_{\Lambda^kT(X)}=H^k(X,\mathbb C)\); a heat-equation proof is attributed informally to ``Moren.
statement: For a closed smooth Riemannian manifold, the map from harmonic complex \(k\)-forms to their de Rham classes is an isomorphism \(\mathcal H^k(X)\simeq H^k_{\mathrm{dR}}(X;\mathbb C)\). Every cohomology class has a unique harmonic representative. A manifold with boundary requires appropriate absolute or relative boundary conditions and a corresponding cohomology theory.
reconstruction: The equality is a canonical isomorphism, not equality of sets. No specific Moren/Maurin book or heat proof is identified from the surname alone.
fate: The Hodge example is used in \citet[\S1.3, examples~7--8]{dynin1966index}.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026, this remains an established construction under the stated hypotheses.

title: Local centralizer slice and pointwise enveloping-algebra description
notes: A semisimple \(a\) is fixed; the connected centralizer is called a section meeting every conjugacy class once. The notes write \(\mathfrak z=\{X:\operatorname{ad}_aX=X\}\) and \(D_y\in\mathfrak g\) for the left-invariant operator agreeing with a differential operator \(D\) at \(y\).
statement: Use \(\mathfrak z=\ker(\operatorname{Ad}(a)-1)\). Left trivialization identifies the value of an order-\(m\) differential operator at \(y\) with an element \(D_y\in U_{\le m}(\mathfrak g_{\mathbb C})\); smoothly varying \(D_y\) describes \(D\). The centralizer provides a redundant local descent submanifold on the regularity domain, not a global one-point-per-orbit cross-section.
reconstruction: Here \(\operatorname{Ad}\), rather than the Lie-algebra map \(\operatorname{ad}\), acts because \(a\in G\). The notation \(\mathfrak g\) for the enveloping algebra is explicitly clarified on P000194. Weyl-group ambiguity survives on a Cartan section.
fate: This is the classical descent framework of \citet{harishchandra1965group}; the exact source lemma was not read.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026, this remains an established construction under the stated hypotheses.

title: The representation sigma and the transfer operator Gamma
notes: The formula is \(\Gamma_y(u\otimes v)=\sigma_y(u)v\), with \(\sigma_y(X)v=\operatorname{Ad}(y^{-1})X\,v-vX\). It is used to replace operators in the two variables of \(f(xyx^{-1})\) by one operator in \(y\).
statement: For fixed \(y\in G\), the map \(X\mapsto L_{\operatorname{Ad}(y^{-1})X}-R_X\) is a Lie-algebra representation on \(U(\mathfrak g_{\mathbb C})\), hence extends to its enveloping algebra. Define the bilinear transfer \(\Gamma_y(u\otimes v)=\sigma_y(u)v\). With the notebook's invariant differentiation convention it encodes \(f(x;u:y;v)=f(x:y;\Gamma_y(u\otimes v))\).
reconstruction: The left and right multiplications act on the enveloping algebra. Their commutators have opposite signs, which is essential to the representation identity. For descent at \(ay\), use \(\Gamma_{ay}\).
fate: The construction is expository Harish-Chandra descent, \citet{harishchandra1965group}; publication matching of this formula is partial.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026, this remains an established construction under the stated hypotheses.

title: PBW leading term and the transverse decomposition
notes: The leading term of \(\Gamma_y(X_1\cdots X_r\otimes Y_1\cdots Y_s)\) is the product of \(X'_i=(\operatorname{Ad}(y^{-1})-1)X_i\) and the \(Y_j\). A complement \(\mathfrak g=\mathfrak z+\mathfrak q\), stable under \(\mathfrak z\), is introduced, and \(\Gamma_y\) is declared an isomorphism on the corresponding generated spaces.
statement: Choose an \(\operatorname{Ad}(a)\)-stable complement \(\mathfrak q\) to \(\mathfrak z\), also stable under the connected centralizer. Identify \(S(\mathfrak q)\) with its symmetrized PBW subspace in \(U(\mathfrak g_{\mathbb C})\). For \(y\in\Xi'\), \[\Gamma_{ay}:S(\mathfrak q_{\mathbb C})\otimes U(\mathfrak z_{\mathbb C})\longrightarrow U(\mathfrak g_{\mathbb C})\] is a filtered vector-space isomorphism: its associated graded is multiplication after the invertible transformation \((\operatorname{Ad}((ay)^{-1})-1)|_{\mathfrak q}\).
reconstruction: The space generated by \(\mathfrak q\) must mean the PBW symmetric subspace, not the associative subalgebra: \(\mathfrak q\) need not be a Lie subalgebra. The displayed leading-term equality holds modulo lower filtration. If \(X\) commutes with \(y\), this leading term vanishes, whereas \(\sigma_y(X)=[X,\cdot]\) need not vanish.
fate: This is the filtered-algebra mechanism of the cited 1965 descent construction, \citet{harishchandra1965group}.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026, this remains an established construction under the stated hypotheses.

title: Radial part as the constant transverse coefficient
notes: On \(a\Xi\), \(\Delta=\delta_{a,G/\Xi}(D)\) is defined by \(\Delta_{ay}=\alpha(D_{ay})\), where \(D-\alpha(D)\) belongs to \(\Gamma_y(\mathfrak q^+\otimes\mathfrak z)\). It is said to act identically on orbit-constant functions.
statement: On \(a\Xi'\), expand \(D_{ay}\) through the PBW isomorphism of the preceding item and project to the degree-zero \(S(\mathfrak q)\) component. The resulting smooth \(U(\mathfrak z)\)-valued coefficients define the radial operator \(\delta_a(D)\). For a locally conjugation-invariant smooth \(f\), \[(Df)|_{a\Xi'}=\delta_a(D)(f|_{a\Xi'}).\]
reconstruction: The omitted enveloping/symmetric-algebra notation and \(ay\)-dependence are restored. The result concerns invariant functions on the descent domain; it is not restriction of an arbitrary differential operator on arbitrary functions to an arbitrary submanifold.
fate: A classical radial-part construction, \citet{harishchandra1965group}; exact group-paper formula verification remains metadata-level.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026, this remains an established construction under the stated hypotheses.

title: Continuity of fiber integration
notes: The existence and continuity of \(\alpha\mapsto f_\alpha\) are stated in the usual compactly supported smooth topologies. The first line mistakenly repeats \(C_c^\infty(M)\) as the target; the product case integrates over the extra variable.
statement: For a smooth submersion \(\pi:M\to N\) and smooth positive densities, fiber integration is continuous \(\pi_!:C_c^\infty(M)\to C_c^\infty(N)\) in the standard LF test-function topology. On a product with product density it is \((\pi_!\alpha)(y)=\int_P\alpha(y,z)\,dz\); coordinate products and a partition of unity give the general map.
reconstruction: The target is \(N\), as the displayed identity and variable \(y\) already require. This repeats and proves the construction at 1966-119.9 rather than introducing a new research question.
fate: The notebook's local product argument establishes the standard construction used in \citet{harishchandra1965group}.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026, this remains an established construction under the stated hypotheses.

title: Translation-invariant distributions are Haar measures
notes: A lemma says that a generalized function invariant under translations is integration against Haar measure, up to a constant.
statement: On a connected Lie group \(G\), a left-translation-invariant distribution is a constant multiple of left Haar measure. More generally, a distribution on \(G\times V\) invariant under translations of the first factor is uniquely \(dg\otimes S\), with \(S\in\mathcal D'(V)\).
reconstruction: The product form is the parameter version needed below. For reductive \(G\), unimodularity removes a left/right Haar distinction; the formulation still specifies left invariance.
fate: An elementary, preexisting ingredient of the descent exposition \citep{harishchandra1965group}.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026, this remains an established construction under the stated hypotheses.

title: The descended distribution sigma_T
notes: Pulling \(T\) back through \(\varphi(x,y)=xayx^{-1}\) gives \(T'\), translation invariant in the first variable; hence \(T'=1\otimes\sigma_T\).
statement: For invariant \(T\) on the open image of the descent submersion, \(\varphi^*T\) is invariant under left translations of its first factor. Fix Haar density \(dg\); then a unique \(\sigma_T\in\mathcal D'(\Xi')\) satisfies \(\varphi^*T=dg\otimes\sigma_T\), under the chosen product-density convention. For \(\gamma\in C_c^\infty(G)\) with \(\int\gamma dg=1\), \[\langle\sigma_T,\beta\rangle=\langle T,\varphi_!(\gamma\otimes\beta)\rangle.\]
reconstruction: The final formula is the valid fiber-integration interpretation, not a literal substitution of \(a^{-1}z^{-1}xz\) into a function defined only on the centralizer.
fate: Classical Harish-Chandra descent, with the group-paper bibliographic identification \citep{harishchandra1965group}.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026, this remains an established construction under the stated hypotheses.

title: The rejected explicit formula for descent
notes: The notebook proposes \(\langle\sigma_T,\beta\rangle=\langle T,\int_G\gamma(z)\beta(a^{-1}z^{-1}xz)dz\rangle\), then adds \ru{Она не имеет смысла} (``It has no meaning''). A diagonal dashed line crosses the formula region.
statement: As written, the formula is undefined: \(\beta\) is a test function on \(\Xi\), but \(a^{-1}z^{-1}xz\) is generally not in \(\Xi\). Arbitrary extensions of \(\beta\) do not repair it canonically. The correct test function on \(G\) is \(\varphi_!(\gamma\otimes\beta)\), defined by integration along fibers and its Jacobian, as in the preceding item.
reconstruction: The notebook's own objection is preserved. The diagonal line's function as cancellation or connector remains uncertain; the mathematical type mismatch does not depend on that palaeographic choice.
fate: An abandoned formula inside an established descent construction \citep{harishchandra1965group}; it is not an unsolved theorem.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026, the literal formula is invalid. The fiber-integral definition supplies the established replacement.

title: Intertwining radial operators with descended distributions
notes: The lemma is \(\sigma_{DT}=\Delta\sigma_T\), with \(\Delta=\delta_{a,G/\Xi}(D)\); the notes emphasize the use of \(\Gamma_{ay}\).
statement: For an invariant differential operator \(D\), Harish-Chandra descent intertwines its action on invariant distributions with the corresponding radial operator on the centralizer. If distributions are defined by duality using densities, the radial operator on distributions must be defined with the compatible formal transpose and density conjugation. With those conventions, \(\sigma_{DT}=\delta_a(D)\sigma_T\).
reconstruction: The smooth-function radial identity alone does not justify using the same coefficient expression on distributions with arbitrary densities. The compatible transpose convention is an essential supplied hypothesis.
fate: The identity belongs to the cited 1965 group descent argument \citep{harishchandra1965group}; its exact printed lemma was not verified.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026, this remains an established construction under the stated hypotheses.

title: Finite central codimension survives descent
notes: The notes say the central operators' images generate an ideal of finite codimension in \(Z(U(\mathfrak z))\), and display an ideal mapping from \(Z(U(\mathfrak g))\) to \(Z(U(\mathfrak z))\).
statement: After the appropriate Harish-Chandra radial conjugation, the centralizer homomorphism identifies the relevant centers with \(S(\mathfrak h)^W\subset S(\mathfrak h)^{W_{\mathfrak z}}\). This is a finite extension. Consequently, if \(J\subset Z(U(\mathfrak g))\) has finite codimension, its extended ideal in \(Z(U(\mathfrak z))\) has finite codimension and annihilates the descended distribution.
reconstruction: It is the image of the annihilating ideal, not the entire center, whose extension matters; the entire unital center already contains \(1\). The displayed raw radial operator includes conjugations not recorded in the notebook's schematic center diagram.
fate: This is the finite-invariant-algebra step in classical descent \citep{harishchandra1965group}.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026, this remains an established construction under the stated hypotheses.

title: Recovering local integrability after descent
notes: The notes conclude \(\sigma_T\in L^1_{\mathrm{loc}}\Rightarrow T\in L^1_{\mathrm{loc}}\), then translate a central \(a\) to the identity and refer to special techniques in three Harish-Chandra papers.
statement: On the image of a surjective submersion, local product coordinates show that a distribution is locally integrable if its pullback is locally integrable. Since \(\varphi^*T=dg\otimes\sigma_T\), local integrability of \(\sigma_T\) gives that of \(T\) near the chosen semisimple orbit. Noncentral descent reduces dimension; central translation, exponential comparison, and the nilpotent analysis complete the regularity theorem.
reconstruction: The statement is local on the covered image. This induction step does not supply the omitted nilpotent proof or identify exactly which three papers the shorthand counts.
fate: The completed regularity proof predates the lecture: \citet[Introduction; Theorem~1]{harishchandra1965algebra}.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026, this remains an established construction under the stated hypotheses.

title: Local integrability of Lorentz-invariant polynomial wave solutions
notes: For \(q=x^2+y^2-z^2\), \(T\) is invariant under transformations preserving \(q\), and \(P(\partial_x^2+\partial_y^2-\partial_z^2)T=0\). The notes ask: is \(T\) locally summable?
statement: Let \(T\in\mathcal D'(\mathbb R^3)\) be invariant under \(SO_0(2,1)\), and let \(0\ne P\in\mathbb C[t]\) satisfy \(P(\Box)T=0\), where \(\Box=\partial_x^2+\partial_y^2-\partial_z^2\). Then \(T\in L^1_{\mathrm{loc}}(\mathbb R^3)\). Full \(O(2,1)\)-invariance is more than needed.
reconstruction: A linear identification with \(\mathfrak{sl}_2(\mathbb R)\) identifies \(q\), up to a nonzero scalar, with its invariant quadratic form. The adjoint group is \(SO_0(2,1)\), and the invariant constant-coefficient algebra is generated by \(\Box\); \((P)\) has finite codimension. The nonzero-polynomial hypothesis is essential.
fate: Already covered by \citet[Theorem~1; \S2]{harishchandra1965algebra}; the notebook question is an expository specialization.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026, the answer is affirmative. It is not a surviving open regularity problem.

title: Why the invariant system is elliptic away from the null cone
notes: The notes say that away from \(q=0\) the system is elliptic, referring to invariant equations plus the polynomial in the wave operator.
statement: On each regular orbit component with \(q\ne0\), an invariant local function or distribution depends on the transverse variable \(s=q\). The radial expression is \(\Box f(q)=4q f''(q)+6f'(q)\). Thus a nonzero polynomial in \(\Box\) yields an ordinary differential equation whose leading coefficient is nonzero for \(q\ne0\). This proves analytic regularity there; the null cone, including its vertex, requires the invariant-distribution theorem.
reconstruction: This is ellipticity after orbit reduction, or of the full invariant system; the scalar wave operator is not elliptic on \(\mathbb R^3\). \oursComputed\ The radial formula is an elementary reconstruction checked by applying the chain rule separately to all three coordinates.
fate: The general regular-set argument appears in \citet[\S2, Lemma~1]{harishchandra1965algebra}.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026, this remains an established construction under the stated hypotheses.

title: Diffeomorphisms of the sphere fixing three points
notes: For \(X=S^2\), the notes give \(\operatorname{Diff}_0X=G\times\operatorname{Diff}(S^2-a,b,c)\), where \(G\) is the conformal group and the second factor is contractible; the three points are to stay fixed.
statement: Give smooth diffeomorphism groups the \(C^\infty\) topology. For three ordered distinct points \(a,b,c\in S^2\), the subgroup of orientation-preserving diffeomorphisms fixing them pointwise is contractible, and composition gives a homeomorphism \[\operatorname{Diff}_0(S^2)\simeq PSL_2(\mathbb C)\times\operatorname{Diff}_0(S^2;a,b,c).\] Consequently \(\operatorname{Diff}_0(S^2)\) has the homotopy type of \(SO(3)\).
reconstruction: The puncture notation means fixed marked points, not arbitrary diffeomorphisms of an open punctured surface. The product is a homeomorphism of spaces, not generally a direct-product decomposition of groups.
fate: \citet[Theorem~1(a)]{earleeells1967diffeomorphism}, communicated 6 February 1967, printed July 1967. The notebook explicitly reports Earle--Eells; separate public circulation before March was not established.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026, this remains an established construction under the stated hypotheses.

title: Diffeomorphisms of the torus fixing one point
notes: For \(X=T^2\), the notes give \(\operatorname{Diff}_0(T^2)=T^2\times\operatorname{Diff}(T^2-a)\), with the fixed-point factor contractible.
statement: The evaluation at a point and the translation action identify \(\operatorname{Diff}_0(T^2)\) homeomorphically with \(T^2\times\operatorname{Diff}_0(T^2;a)\). The subgroup fixing \(a\) and homotopic to the identity is contractible. Thus \(\operatorname{Diff}_0(T^2)\simeq T^2\).
reconstruction: Homotopy to the identity is part of the fixed-point subgroup; arbitrary mapping classes fixing the point are not included.
fate: \citet[Theorem~1(b)]{earleeells1967diffeomorphism}; the manuscript was communicated in February and printed in July 1967; the precise first public circulation is not established.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026, this remains an established construction under the stated hypotheses.

title: Contractibility in genus at least two
notes: For genus at least \(2\), \(\operatorname{Diff}_0X\) is declared contractible.
statement: If \(X\) is a closed, connected, oriented smooth surface of genus \(g\ge2\), its smooth diffeomorphisms homotopic to the identity form the identity component, and this topological group is contractible in the \(C^\infty\) topology.
reconstruction: Closedness, connectedness, and the topology on the group are supplied; boundary and puncture variants are separate statements.
fate: \citet[Theorem~1(c), Corollary]{earleeells1967diffeomorphism}; communicated to the journal in February 1967 and expressly reported as their result in these March notes.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026, this remains an established construction under the stated hypotheses.

title: Quasiconformal uniformization and the Teichmüller fibration
notes: The proof is said to use Ahlfors and Bers on quasiconformal maps, ``onto which any diffeomorphism contracts.
statement: The rigorous strategy uses the contractible space of smooth conformal structures, the contractible Teichm\"uller space, and a principal action of the appropriate identity or marked-point diffeomorphism group. The resulting fibration and the manifold properties of the group imply contractibility of the relevant fiber. Quasiconformal Beltrami equations provide the required parametrization and local sections.
reconstruction: The notes do not describe a literal deformation of every diffeomorphism ``onto quasiconformal maps''; smooth surface diffeomorphisms already are quasiconformal for suitable bounds. The fibration, rather than that phrase, is the substantive argument.
fate: The exact proof outline is \citet[Theorem~2; \S\S3--4]{earleeells1967diffeomorphism}.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026, this remains an established construction under the stated hypotheses.

title: The diffeomorphism group as an infinite-dimensional Lie group
notes: The final sentence calls \(\operatorname{Diff}\) a Lie group in a new sense of smooth structure.
statement: For a compact smooth manifold, \(\operatorname{Diff}(X)\) admits an infinite-dimensional smooth Lie-group structure modeled locally on the Fr\'echet space of smooth vector fields. This requires a suitable infinite-dimensional differentiability calculus; it is not a finite-dimensional Lie group.
reconstruction: The notebook specifies no calculus or regularity theorem. The contemporary reference is Leslie, as cited by Earle--Eells; Leslie's full article was not accessible in this run.
fate: \citet[Remark~2 and reference~8]{earleeells1967diffeomorphism} cites Leslie's then-forthcoming 1967 construction.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026, this remains an established construction under the stated hypotheses.

title: Semiclassical Fourier transformation of the Schrödinger operator
notes: Under the Anosov heading, \(-\tfrac{h^2}{2}\partial_x^2+U(x)\) transforms to \(\tfrac{p^2}{2}+U(\tfrac h i\partial_p)\); the Fourier kernel is \(e^{\pm i\langle x,p\rangle/h}\).
statement: For \(h>0\), use the unitary transform \((\mathcal F_h^+f)(p)=(2\pi h)^{-1/2}\int e^{ixp/h}f(x)\,dx\). On Schwartz functions and for polynomial \(U\), \[\mathcal F_h^+\left(-\frac{h^2}{2}\partial_x^2+U(x)\right)(\mathcal F_h^+)^{-1}=\frac{p^2}{2}+U(-ih\partial_p).\] For a more general potential the notation on the right denotes the corresponding Fourier multiplier/convolution or functional-calculus operator on its appropriate domain.
reconstruction: The positive Fourier sign matches the notebook's \(h/i\). The polynomial/core case supplies a precise statement without assuming an arbitrary potential is a differential operator.
fate: An elementary preexisting Fourier identity, used in Maslov's 1965 programme; only the book's metadata were checked \citep{maslov1965perturbation}.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026, this remains an established construction under the stated hypotheses.
speaker: D. V. Anosov

title: A Fourier transform with a self-adjoint operator as reciprocal Planck constant
notes: For Hilbert space \(H\), self-adjoint \(A\) with \(0\) not an eigenvalue, the notes replace \(1/h\) by \(A\) and insert the normalization \(|A|^{n/2}/(\sqrt{2\pi})^n\) in \(\phi^A f(p)=\int e^{iA\langle x,p\rangle}f(x)\,dx\).
statement: A precise interpretation uses the spectral decomposition \(A=\int\lambda\,dE(\lambda)\), with \(E(\{0\})=0\). On each spectral fiber define \[\mathcal F_\lambda^+f(p)=\left(\frac{|\lambda|}{2\pi}\right)^{n/2}\int_{\mathbb R^n}e^{i\lambda\langle x,p\rangle}f(x)\,dx.\] The direct integral of these unitary transforms defines a unitary \(\mathcal F_A^+\) on \(L^2(\mathbb R^n;H)\). The notebook's integral formula is literal on a suitable spectral/Schwartz core and otherwise is understood through this extension.
reconstruction: \ours\ The direct-integral interpretation is supplied here. It allows \(0\) in continuous spectrum: ``not an eigenvalue'' does not imply \(A^{-1}\) is bounded. Fiberwise Plancherel verifies the normalization; substitution \(q=\lambda p\) independently gives the same norm identity. No exact occurrence of this operator-valued formula was located in the checked Maslov metadata.
fate: Maslov's 1965 book is the stated historical context, but the precise transform-to-publication match is unresolved \citep{maslov1965perturbation}.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026, the spectral construction above is well defined. The attribution is only thematic; no new general quantization theorem is inferred.
speaker: D. V. Anosov

title: Formal operator-valued quantization of L(x,p,A inverse)
notes: The note ends with \(\mathcal L(x,\widehat p,A^{-1})f=\overline{\phi^A}_{p\to x}L(x,p,A^{-1})\phi^A_{x\to p}f\), after posing \(Lu=f\) with \(u(x)\in H\). No symbol estimates, domain, ordering convention, or solvability theorem is supplied.
statement: As a formal quantization rule the expression indicates applying an \(A\)-scaled Fourier transform, a symbol, and inverse transformation with \(x\) retained as an external parameter. It does not define a unique operator for arbitrary noncommuting operator-valued \(L\). A rigorous restricted construction is possible when \(L\) is decomposable with respect to \(A\), its scalar spectral fibers satisfy stated pseudodifferential symbol bounds, and common domains and an ordering convention are fixed.
reconstruction: The decomposability and symbol assumptions describe one possible implementation, not a recovered claim by Anosov. The unresolved issue here is the missing statement, not a demonstrated open research problem.
fate: The Maslov book provides a thematic lead only; neither its catalogue nor the notebook identifies this general theorem \citep{maslov1965perturbation}.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026, the unrestricted construction and the intended solvability result remain unidentified from these notes.
speaker: D. V. Anosov

title: Regular algebraic actions and orbits
notes: A regular map \(\sigma:G\times X\to X\) is illustrated by an associativity square, whose top arrow is labelled \(\sigma\times1\); equivalent points form an orbit.
statement: Over an algebraically closed field \(k\), an algebraic action of an algebraic group \(G\) on a variety \(X\) is a morphism \(\sigma:G\times X\to X\) satisfying \(\sigma(e,x)=x\) and \(\sigma(g,\sigma(h,x))=\sigma(gh,x)\). In the standard ordered product \(G\times G\times X\), the top map of the associativity square is \(1_G\times\sigma\).
reconstruction: The identity axiom is supplied. The stated top-arrow label has the wrong factor order unless a permutation of factors is additionally declared.
fate: Standard setup in the 1965 book \citep{mumford1965invariant}; modern definitions are in \citet[\S2.1]{berczi2016quotients}.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026, this remains an established construction under the stated hypotheses.

title: When does an orbit set admit an algebraic quotient?
notes: The explicit question is when \(X/G\), meaning the set of orbits, is an algebraic variety and in what sense the map \(X\to X/G\) is regular.
statement: For an affine variety \(X\) over an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero and a reductive algebraic group \(G\), the invariant ring is finitely generated and \(q:X\to\operatorname{Spec}k[X]^G\) is a categorical quotient. Its fibers identify orbit-closure equivalence classes and contain one closed orbit; it is a geometric orbit quotient of all \(X\) precisely when all orbits are closed. For an arbitrary algebraic action, a geometric quotient exists on a suitable nonempty invariant open subset; it need not exist on all of \(X\).
reconstruction: Affine reductive hypotheses make the notes' final criterion precise. The distinction between a categorical quotient and a quotient whose fibers are individual orbits is essential. These are answers to definite versions of the stated question, not an assertion of a single universal global quotient theorem for all varieties.
fate: Known before the report from Mumford/Rosenlicht; compare \citet[Theorems~2.1.10, 2.2.1]{berczi2016quotients}.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026, the stated affine reductive question and the generic-open existence theorem are established. The unrestricted wording needs a chosen quotient category.

title: Unlabelled orbit-space counterexample sketch
notes: A drawing of axes and curved branches accompanies the statement that no algebraic structure can be introduced until a point is removed. Neither the group, action, variety, nor removed point is labelled.
statement: There is insufficient information to state a unique example or a counterexample. The picture is consistent with several torus actions having nonclosed orbits, but neither the orbit partition nor the intended separation condition can be recovered.
reconstruction: The familiar action \(t\cdot(x,y)=(tx,t^{-1}y)\) is not installed as the missing example: even there, deleting the origin has subtleties involving nonseparated orbit spaces.
fate: The general quotient literature \citep[\S2.1]{berczi2016quotients} does not identify an unlabelled diagram.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026, this particular example remains unidentified; it does not establish an orphan open problem.

title: Semicontinuity of stabilizer and orbit dimensions
notes: The stationary subgroup may have larger dimension than the generic stationary subgroup.
statement: For an algebraic group acting on a variety, the function \(x\mapsto\dim G_x\) is upper semicontinuous, and \(\dim(Gx)=\dim G-\dim G_x\) is lower semicontinuous. On an irreducible variety the generic stabilizer dimension is minimal and the generic orbit dimension maximal.
reconstruction: Dimension is meant scheme-theoretically or geometrically consistently; the characteristic-zero setting in the notes avoids nonreduced stabilizer complications.
fate: Classical action geometry; see \citet[\S2.2, discussion preceding Theorem~2.2.1]{berczi2016quotients}.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026, this remains an established construction under the stated hypotheses.

title: Necessary conditions on a regular morphism with orbit fibers
notes: If \(X/G\) has an algebraic structure and \(X\to X/G\) is regular, all orbits must have the same dimension and, in particular, be closed.
statement: Let \(X,Y\) be irreducible varieties over an algebraically closed field, and let \(q:X\to Y\) be a surjective morphism whose set-theoretic fibers over closed points are exactly the \(G\)-orbits. Then all such orbits are closed and have dimension \(\dim X-\dim Y\). Indeed fiber dimension is at least this number, while orbit dimension is at most its generic value, which equals it.
reconstruction: \ours\ Irreducibility, surjectivity, and the single-orbit fiber condition make the notebook claim valid. Closedness follows directly from being a fiber, not merely from equal orbit dimensions. Independently, the generic fiber-dimension theorem and stabilizer semicontinuity give the two opposite inequalities, checking the argument.
fate: A standard consequence of algebraic orbit and fiber dimensions in the quotient framework \citep[\S2.1]{berczi2016quotients}.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026, this remains an established construction under the stated hypotheses.

title: Closed orbits and the affine reductive geometric quotient
notes: For a reductive group in characteristic zero, the notes end with ``a quotient exists if and only if all orbits are closed.
statement: If \(G\) is reductive, \(\operatorname{char}k=0\), and \(X\) is affine, the invariant quotient \(q:X\to X/\!/G\) exists whether or not every orbit is closed. It is geometric, with precisely one orbit in each fiber, if and only if every orbit is closed. Closedness alone is not the stated existence criterion for an arbitrary nonaffine variety or for an unspecified quotient category.
reconstruction: The missing words are ``affine'' and ``geometric.'' The literal statement is false when ``quotient'' means categorical quotient. This distinguishes a valid old theorem in shorthand from a new existence problem.
fate: The precise affine theorem is \citet[Theorem~2.2.1]{berczi2016quotients}, reflecting the prelecture Mumford theory \citep{mumford1965invariant}.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026, this remains an established construction under the stated hypotheses.

title: Compactly supported stable symbol classes
notes: \(\Sigma(\mathbb R^n)\) consists of maps \(\mathbb R^n\times S^{n-1}\to GL_\infty(\mathbb C)\), equal to \(1\) outside \(K\times S^{n-1}\). The general version uses \(T_0(X)\) and a compact support in the base.
statement: A stable invertible principal symbol on \(X\), trivial outside a compact subset of the base, is represented by a map \(S^*X\to GL_N(\mathbb C)\), stabilized by identity blocks and considered through homotopy and the relation of extending from the base. Clutching over the cotangent disk bundle yields its compactly supported \(K\)-theory symbol class in \(K_c^0(T^*X)\). A metric identifies tangent and cotangent sphere bundles when necessary.
reconstruction: The raw maps are not themselves already all of \(K_c^0(T^*X)\); the relations and, for general bundles, bundle-valued symbols are needed. \(T_0\) is interpreted as the punctured cotangent bundle with degree-zero homogeneity, or equivalently its cosphere.
fate: Stable symbol and \(K\)-theory framework: \citet[\S2; \S3.1]{dynin1966index}.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026, this remains an established construction under the stated hypotheses.

title: Homotopy invariance and direct-sum additivity do not determine the index
notes: Above a dividing line the notes claim a unique \(\operatorname{ind}:\Sigma(\mathbb R^n)\to\mathbb Z\) with only (I) homotopy invariance and (II) direct-sum additivity.
statement: These two axioms alone cannot normalize a nonzero index: the zero map and every integer multiple of any additive homotopy invariant satisfy them. Already for \(n=1\), \[w(\sigma)=\operatorname{wind}\det\sigma(\cdot,+1)-\operatorname{wind}\det\sigma(\cdot,-1)\] is a nonzero such invariant for compactly supported stable symbols; \(0,w,2w\) are distinct.
reconstruction: \ours\ The counterexample uses a smooth phase that rises from \(0\) to \(2\pi\) in a compact interval on the positive component and is constant on the negative component. Determinant multiplication under direct sum proves additivity; homotopy invariance follows from integer winding. The later normalization axiom fixes this defect.
fate: Dynin's actual index properties include a normalization: \citet[\S3.1; \S3.2.10]{dynin1966index}.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026, the isolated uniqueness statement is false; the normalized index theory remains established.

title: Multiplicativity under external products
notes: A product \(\#:\Sigma(X)\times\Sigma(Y)\to\Sigma(X\times Y)\) satisfies \(\operatorname{ind}(\sigma_X\#\sigma_Y)=\operatorname{ind}\sigma_X\operatorname{ind}\sigma_Y\).
statement: For compactly supported elliptic \(K\)-theory symbols, their external product corresponds to the graded tensor product of elliptic complexes. The analytic index is multiplicative on this product, as is the topological index. The symbol product is not merely pointwise multiplication of two unrelated square matrices on different cosphere bundles.
reconstruction: The external-product construction is supplied; the notes state only its name and index identity. Stable triviality of tangent bundles is part of the lecture's restricted family, not a necessary hypothesis of the modern product theorem.
fate: \citet[\S3.1.6]{dynin1966index} gives the prelecture product property.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026, this remains an established construction under the stated hypotheses.

title: Excision for compactly supported index classes
notes: If \(\operatorname{supp}\sigma\subset U\subset X\), the index on \(U\) equals the index on \(X\).
statement: For an open embedding \(j:U\hookrightarrow X\) and a compactly supported elliptic symbol class \(a\in K_c^0(T^*U)\), extension by the identity/zero symbol class defines \(j_!a\), and \(\operatorname{ind}_X(j_!a)=\operatorname{ind}_U(a)\). The relevant support is the nontrivial part of the symbol class, not the support of an everywhere invertible matrix as a function.
reconstruction: This is an index statement for symbols trivial at infinity; an arbitrary differential operator on a noncompact open manifold need not be Fredholm without this interpretation.
fate: A standard topological-index property in the framework of \citet[\S\S2--3]{dynin1966index}; exact six-axiom wording was not found there.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026, this remains an established construction under the stated hypotheses.

title: Symbols pulled back from the base have zero index
notes: A commuting diagram \(T_0(X)\to X\to GL\) implies \(\operatorname{ind}\sigma=0\).
statement: An invertible symbol that extends over the cotangent disk bundle, in particular one pulled back from a bundle automorphism on \(X\), has zero relative \(K\)-theory class and zero index. Analytically, multiplication by the corresponding invertible bundle map is an invertible order-zero realization.
reconstruction: The compact-support/trivial-at-infinity convention from the definition is retained. This explains why raw homotopy classes on the cosphere require a quotient by extendible symbols.
fate: An elementary consequence of the symbol construction in \citet[\S2]{dynin1966index}.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026, this remains an established construction under the stated hypotheses.

title: One-dimensional winding normalization
notes: For \(X=\mathbb R\), the Noether--Muskhelishvili formula is \(\operatorname{ind}\sigma=(2\pi)^{-1}\Delta_{\mathbb R\times S^0}\arg\det\sigma\).
statement: For a smooth stable invertible symbol equal to the identity off a compact subset of \(\mathbb R\), each of its two cosphere components closes to a loop. With the boundary orientation and Fourier/index sign convention chosen consistently, the index is the oriented difference of their determinant winding numbers. Reversing the Fourier or boundary orientation convention reverses the displayed sign.
reconstruction: The unoriented notation \(\mathbb R\times S^0\) is insufficient to determine the sign; no independent sign is silently imposed on the notebook.
fate: The normalized dimension-one calculation is \citet[\S3.2.10]{dynin1966index}.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026, this remains an established construction under the stated hypotheses.

title: A normalized index characterization on stably parallelizable manifolds
notes: Below the line, the notes assert existence and uniqueness of an index for manifolds with stably trivial tangent bundle satisfying (I)--(VI).
statement: The intended object is the normalized index homomorphism on compactly supported stable elliptic symbol classes, natural under excision and external products and normalized on the one-dimensional Bott generator. In a precise \(K\)-theoretic axiomatization, Bott periodicity and compatible pushforward determine the usual topological index, equal to the analytic index. The six shorthand lines require a specified symbol category, product construction, and stabilization before a literal uniqueness theorem can be tested.
reconstruction: The modern normalized index statement is supplied as an interpretation. No exact proof of the notebook's six-axiom formulation, restricted to stably parallelizable manifolds, was located in the opened Dynin exposition; it is therefore not reported as a verbatim published theorem.
fate: The 1966 exposition proves the index formula and required properties \citep[\S3.2.1]{dynin1966index}; the exact axiom list matches only partially.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026, the normalized analytic/topological index is established. The bare six-line formulation is under-specified, not evidence of an open uniqueness problem.

title: Normal matrix factorization and partial indices
notes: The factorization is \(A(\omega,\eta_n)=A_-M_-M_+A_+\), with \(M_+=\operatorname{diag}((\eta_n+i)^{n_j(\omega)})\). The integers \(n_j\) may depend on \(\omega\). In the full variables \(A_\pm\) have degree zero and the order factor \(\xi_-^\alpha\) is included in \(M_-\).
statement: For an elliptic matrix symbol, homogeneous of order \(\alpha+i\beta\) and with the regularity and normal-limit assumptions of the convolution calculus, fix a nonzero tangential direction \(\omega\). Remove the scalar order and normal-jump factors; the normalized matrix admits Wiener--Hopf factorization with integer partial indices \(n_j(\omega)\). The unreduced partial indices are \(\kappa_j=n_j+\gamma_j\), where \(\gamma_j\) arise from a chosen logarithm of the normal jump. Such pointwise factorizations need not vary continuously when the integer indices change.
reconstruction: The normalization, half-plane analyticity of the factors, and distinction between integer and full partial indices are supplied. No continuously chosen factorization is inferred from pointwise factorization.
fate: The pointwise factorization was already available: \citet[\S4]{vishikeskin1967elliptic}, received December 1965; the later notation is exact in \citet[\S1.3]{vishikeskin1967normally}.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026, this remains an established construction under the stated hypotheses.

title: Fredholm normal families despite jumping kernel dimensions
notes: The notes emphasize \(n_j(\omega)\) need not be constant and nevertheless assert a regularizer construction; the dimensions are denoted \(m_+(\omega)\) and \(m_-(\omega)\).
statement: Let \(A_\omega\) be the half-line convolution family obtained by freezing the boundary point and unit tangential covector. Choose Sobolev orders avoiding the critical values \(\operatorname{Re}\kappa_j+\tfrac12+\mathbb Z\), continuously over the parameter set, and identify the resulting spaces with fixed Hilbert spaces. Under the stated symbol regularity, \(A_\omega\) is a norm-continuous Fredholm family. Its kernel and cokernel dimensions \(m_+\) and \(m_-\) can jump, but their difference is constant on each connected component and both dimensions are bounded on a compact parameter space.
reconstruction: Uniform admissibility of the Sobolev order is essential; arbitrary elliptic symbols and arbitrary orders are not covered. Continuity concerns the Fredholm operators, not a chosen kernel basis or factorization.
fate: The corresponding result is \citet[\S1, Lemmas~1.1--3.1 and Remark~1.1]{vishikeskin1967normally}, received 27 April 1967 and published that year.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026, the qualified family theorem is established. Its verified 1967 proof expressly removes the earlier constant-integer-index restriction.

title: Auxiliary potentials and boundary equations
notes: The one-dimensional system is \(Au_++G\rho=\ell f+u_-\), \((B,u_+)_{\eta_n}+E\rho=g\), with \(\rho\in\mathbb C^M\), \(\ell-M=m_+-m_-\), unique solvability, and a continuously dependent inverse \(R_\omega\). The same glyph \(\ell\) is used for extension of \(f\) and for the number of boundary equations.
statement: For a continuous Fredholm family \(A_\omega:H_1\to H_2\), seek a block completion \[\mathcal A_\omega=\begin{pmatrix}A_\omega&G_\omega\\B_\omega&E_\omega\end{pmatrix}:H_1\oplus\mathbb C^M\longrightarrow H_2\oplus\mathbb C^\ell\] that is invertible. A necessary index balance is \(\ell-M=\operatorname{ind}A_\omega\). Such completions exist locally in the parameter; once the block is norm-continuous and invertible, \(R_\omega=\mathcal A_\omega^{-1}\) is norm-continuous. In the convolution problem, \(G\) is a potential matrix and \(B\) a boundary functional with prescribed homogeneity and Sobolev mapping properties. The index balance alone does not ensure a single global completion.
reconstruction: The undefined boundary-restriction subscript on \(g\) is not used to recover a new space. Abstract local completion and continuity of inversion explain the claim; global existence is separated as the later explicit question.
fate: The same augmented system and algebraic solvability condition appear in \citet[\S1.5, equations (44.1)--(45.1)]{vishikeskin1967normally}.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026, this completion construction and its parameter continuity are standard under the stated assumptions; the global obstruction is recorded separately.

title: Homogeneous lifting and localization of normal inverses
notes: The normal construction is transferred to \(n\) dimensions by factoring out \(|\xi'|\); left and right regularizers are obtained by localization. The margin adds \ru{Якобы} beside the reference to Simonenko's abstract treatment of inverse operators depending on parameters.
statement: Suppose an elliptic convolution system on a smooth bounded domain has an admissible continuous normal family and globally specified potential/boundary symbols of the required orders, whose augmented normal problem is invertible at every boundary covector. Rescaling the normal inverse by tangential homogeneity and patching local parametrices yields left and right regularizers modulo compact operators on the designated Sobolev spaces. Hence the global boundary system is Fredholm. A formal collection of pointwise inverses without symbol estimates, admissible orders, and compatible global completion is insufficient.
reconstruction: The hypotheses are those of the matching theorem, not an assertion that arbitrary parameter dependence can be localized. The marginal reservation is retained as evidence, not interpreted as a refutation of Simonenko.
fate: The precise half-space and bounded-domain results are in \citet[pp.~316, 322--325]{vishikeskin1967normally}. Simonenko's 1965 paper is a metadata-verified lead only \citep{simonenko1965method}.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026, the qualified Fredholm construction is established. The exact Simonenko passage meant by the speaker remains unverified.

title: Normal jump logarithms and admissible Sobolev orders
notes: Under the heading \ru{Эскин}, the notes set \(a_\pm(x')=A(x',0,0,\pm1)\), \(b=a_+^{-1}a_-\), and \(\gamma=(2\pi i)^{-1}\log b\). They demand globally continuous eigenvalue branches with \(|\operatorname{Re}\gamma_i-\operatorname{Re}\gamma_j|<1\), calling this \(\widehat{\mathcal E}_\alpha\). The jump is called a measure of nonellipticity.
statement: For a zero-order normalized elliptic symbol at a smooth boundary, the two invertible normal limits define a normal jump \(b=a_+^{-1}a_-\). Locally one can choose a matrix logarithm and spectral branches in a strip of width less than one. Global branch choices require compatibility. For nonzero symbol order, first normalize the order; in Vishik--Eskin's convention the negative limit includes the phase \(e^{i\pi(\alpha+i\beta)}\). A continuous Sobolev-order function avoiding all critical fractional indices is the functional-analytic admissibility condition.
reconstruction: The jump measures normal factorization data, not a failure of interior ellipticity. The notebook's symbol for the class is uncertain, and its global enumeration of eigenvalue branches is stronger than a merely pointwise logarithm. The later paper uses a precisely defined class and a noncritical order condition rather than relying on this compressed name.
fate: The normalized limits and admissibility condition are explicit in \citet[\S2, equations (1.2)--(6.2)]{vishikeskin1967normally}; local logarithmic factorization predates the lecture \citep[\S4]{vishikeskin1967elliptic}.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026, the normalized construction is established; the notebook's class label has only a partial exact identification.

title: Diagonal systems and the limitation of a common ordinary space
notes: For diagonal \(A=\operatorname{diag}(a_j)\), the notes write scalar factorization indices \(\kappa_j(x')\), \(b=e^{2\pi i\kappa_j}\), \(\gamma_j=\kappa_j\), and say the class need not contain the system. The qualification is ``operators in ordinary spaces.
statement: For a diagonal system the full scalar factorization indices need not lie in a common real strip of width one when one insists on a fixed compatible choice and common Sobolev scale. The eigenvalues of the normal jump determine \(\kappa_j\) only modulo integers; in general \(\gamma_j\equiv\kappa_j\pmod{\mathbb Z}\), not equality for every logarithm branch. Different component orders or variable admissible orders can alter the functional setting, so this observation is a limitation of a specified common-space class, not of elliptic diagonal systems as such.
reconstruction: The scalar index glyph is read provisionally as \(\kappa\). The equation \(\gamma_j=\kappa_j\) is meaningful only after choosing compatible branches. Pointwise branch adjustment can always narrow a finite set of fractional parts; the possible difficulty is global compatibility with the intended spaces.
fate: The distinction between \(n_j\), \(\gamma_j\), and \(\kappa_j\) is explicit in \citet[\S1.3, p.~306; \S2.1]{vishikeskin1967normally}; the notebook's example lacks full symbols.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026, this is an understood qualification of the formulation. No particular diagonal counterexample can be uniquely recovered.

title: Global completion of the boundary Fredholm family
notes: The final line asks when there globally exist \(G\) and an overwritten expression involving \(E\), ``(and \(B\)).'' The connective between \(G\) and \(E\) is not legible enough to decide among the transcription's alternatives. The preceding normal system fixes the mathematical context.
statement: In the admissible Vishik--Eskin convolution calculus on a smooth bounded domain with compact boundary \(\Gamma\), let \(A_\gamma\), \(\gamma\in S^*\Gamma\), be the normalized continuous Fredholm family, of constant numerical index \(N\). When do globally defined finite matrices of potential and boundary symbols give an invertible normal completion using trivial auxiliary bundles? The precise criterion is \[\operatorname{Ind}(A) = N[1]\quad\hbox{in }K^0(S^*\Gamma).\] Under the paper's regularity and noncritical-order hypotheses this is necessary and sufficient, and the completion can be chosen with \(E=0\). For a connected parameter space, this says that the reduced family-index class vanishes.
reconstruction: This identifies the definite completion question from the system on P000202; it does not resolve the overwritten connective. Trivial auxiliary bundles, admissible symbol orders, and constant numerical index are essential. Allowing arbitrary auxiliary bundles changes the obstruction. Necessity for a block with \(E\ne0\) also follows from its family index; sufficiency follows from the stronger \(E=0\) construction.
fate: A direct contextual match is \citet[\S3, Theorems~1.3 and 2.3, pp.~328--331]{vishikeskin1967normally}, received 27 April 1967, after this lecture.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026, this precise global completion question was solved in 1967. The printed theorem matches the augmented system, jumping indices, global symbols, and obstruction; the source's ambiguous connective prevents a claim of verbatim equivalence.

title: Strict hyperbolicity of the homogeneous symbol
notes: For a real homogeneous polynomial \(a(\xi_0,\ldots,\xi_n)\) of degree \(m\), every nonzero spatial tuple is required to give exactly \(m\) distinct real roots in \(\xi_0\). The ambient space is first called \(\mathbb R^n\), although \(n+1\) coordinates are then used.
statement: Write \(N=n+1\). A real homogeneous polynomial \(a\) of degree \(m\) on \(\mathbb R^N\) is strictly hyperbolic with respect to \(e_0\) if \(a(e_0)\ne0\) and, for every \(\xi'\ne0\), the polynomial \(t\mapsto a(t,\xi')\) has \(m\) distinct real roots. The corresponding constant-coefficient differential operator is \(P=a(\partial_x)\), with any Fourier convention declared consistently.
reconstruction: Noncharacteristic time direction and the distinction between strict hyperbolicity and the weaker real-root condition are supplied. The dimension is corrected uniformly, not by changing subsequent homology degrees.
fate: Already in \citet[\S1, p.~88]{atiyah1967hyperbolic}, lecture February 1967, print 1968.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026, this remains an established construction under the stated hypotheses.

title: The retarded fundamental solution
notes: The system \(PE=\delta\), \(E=0\) for \(x_0<0\), has a unique solution by uniqueness for the Cauchy problem.
statement: For a real homogeneous strictly hyperbolic operator with noncharacteristic time direction, there is a unique distribution \(E\in\mathcal D'(\mathbb R^N)\) satisfying \(PE=\delta_0\) and \(\operatorname{supp}E\subset\{x_0\ge0\}\). More precisely its support lies in the closed forward propagation cone dual to the chosen hyperbolicity cone. Uniqueness uses the vanishing of a homogeneous solution with past-zero support.
reconstruction: Existence, implicit in ``we seek'' and then ``it is denoted \(E\),'' is distinguished from the stated uniqueness argument. The propagation cone is the convex support cone, a different notion from the projective dual wavefront hypersurface below.
fate: Classical before the report; \citet[\S1, p.~88]{atiyah1967hyperbolic}. A Fourier--Laplace construction is in \citet[\S3]{atiyahbottgarding1970lacunas}.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026, this remains an established construction under the stated hypotheses.

title: Analyticity away from the dual characteristic hypersurface
notes: The characteristic cone \(A=\{a(\xi)=0\}\) has a dual cone \(B=\{b(x)=0\}\), described by tangent hyperplanes. The solution is analytic in every connected component of its complement.
statement: For the generic smooth projective characteristic hypersurface \(A\subset\mathbb{CP}^{N-1}\), let \(B\) be the real cone over its projective dual discriminant in the dual projective space. For real \(x\notin B\), the section \(A_x=A\cap\{x\cdot\xi=0\}\) is transverse. The retarded fundamental solution restricts to a real-analytic function on each connected component of \(\{x_0>0\}\setminus B\). The characteristic cone in covector space and its dual in physical space need not have the same defining polynomial.
reconstruction: ``Dual'' here concerns tangent hyperplanes, not the convex polar cone. The generic complex smoothness is supplied as in the next page; this avoids treating every real tangent-locus description as an exact global algebraic equation without qualification.
fate: The precise geometric setup and analytic statement are in \citet[\S1, pp.~89--91]{atiyah1967hyperbolic}.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026, this remains an established construction under the stated hypotheses.

title: Lacunas and stability under perturbation
notes: A connected component \(C\) is a lacuna if \(E\equiv0\) there; it is stable if this persists for nearby equations.
statement: A component \(C\) of the complement of the wavefront/dual discriminant in the future half-space is a lacuna in the notebook's sense if \(E_a|_C=0\). It is stable if, for a fixed \(x\in C\), all sufficiently small real homogeneous degree-\(m\) perturbations of \(a\) have fundamental solutions vanishing in a neighborhood of \(x\); the definition is independent of the chosen point in \(C\). The comparison is local or on compact subsets of the moving component, not a requirement that the original entire component remain fixed.
reconstruction: The perturbation class and meaning of persistence are supplied. Atiyah--Bott--G\aa rding later use a broader notion of lacuna allowing a regular continuation and call the zero-solution case a strong lacuna; their terminology must not silently replace the notebook's.
fate: Defined by Petrovsky before 1945 \citep[pp.~290--291]{petrovsky1945lacunas}; the formulation follows \citet[pp.~89--90]{atiyah1967hyperbolic}.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026, the definition and its homological criteria are classical. Later terminology is distinguished in \citet[\S9--10]{atiyahbottgarding1970lacunas}.

title: Reduction to a nonsingular complex characteristic hypersurface
notes: The real polynomial defines \(A\subset\mathbb{CP}^n\), assumed to have no complex singularities. The notes say a small real change of coefficients can achieve this.
statement: Strict hyperbolicity is open in the space of real homogeneous degree-\(m\) polynomials. The complex singular-hypersurface discriminant is a proper algebraic subset of that coefficient space. Consequently a strictly hyperbolic polynomial can be approximated by real strictly hyperbolic polynomials with nonsingular complex projective zero locus. This generic reduction is legitimate for a question defined through stability under all sufficiently small admissible perturbations.
reconstruction: Strict hyperbolicity alone already gives smoothness of the real projective zero locus, but not complex smoothness. The reduction does not prove that the original complex variety was nonsingular.
fate: The prelecture reduction is \citet[\S1, p.~90]{atiyah1967hyperbolic}.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026, this remains an established construction under the stated hypotheses.

title: The real hyperplane-section cycle beta
notes: The notes form \(A_x=A\cap\{x\cdot\xi=0\}\), call \((A_x)_{\mathbb R}\) a cycle of dimension \(n-2\), and write \(\beta_x\in H_{n-2}(A_x)\). The phrase ``a sum of spheres'' is attached to this section.
statement: Assume \(N>2\) and \(m,N\) even, with \(A\subset\mathbb{CP}^{N-1}\) smooth and \(x\notin B\). Hyperbolicity gives \(m/2\) spherical components of \(A_{\mathbb R}\), each of real dimension \(N-2\), with compatible orientations from the hyperbolicity direction. A trivialization of the real hyperplane line bundle over \(A_{\mathbb R}\) makes \(x\cdot\xi\) a real function. Its transverse zero locus is oriented and defines \[\beta_x=[(A_x)_{\mathbb R}]\in H_{N-3}(A_x;\mathbb C).\]
reconstruction: The coefficient field and orientation data are restored from the identified source. Atiyah's sphere decomposition concerns \(A_{\mathbb R}\), not a stated decomposition of every \((A_x)_{\mathbb R}\); the notebook's placement of that phrase is not accepted as a general theorem about hyperplane sections.
fate: Exact cycle construction: \citet[\S1, p.~91]{atiyah1967hyperbolic}; the sphere phrase has only a partial match.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026, this remains an established construction under the stated hypotheses.

title: The wave operator: an empty real section, not an empty complex quadric
notes: For \(a=\xi_0^2-\sum_{j=1}^n\xi_j^2\) and \(x=(1,0,\ldots,0)\), the notes obtain \(\xi_0=0\), \(\sum\xi_j^2=0\), then say that in projective space this has no points.
statement: The real projective section is empty because a sum of real squares vanishes only at the zero vector; hence \(\beta_x=0\). The complex projective section is nonempty for \(n\ge2\): for example \([\xi_0:\xi_1:\xi_2:\cdots]=[0:1:i:0:\cdots]\) lies on it. If \(N=n+1>2\) is even, the order \(m=2<N\) and the Petrovsky criterion yields the familiar stable interior lacuna of the retarded wave solution.
reconstruction: \ours\ The explicit complex point checks the literal error independently of the real positive-definiteness argument. The parity and dimension restriction is essential: the empty real section by itself does not assert Huygens' principle in every dimension.
fate: The wave example is classical \citep[p.~289]{petrovsky1945lacunas}; see \citet[pp.~88--89, Theorem~1]{atiyah1967hyperbolic}.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026, the corrected example is standard; the literal claim of no complex points is false for the dimensions used in the theorem.

title: The signed relative cycle alpha and its boundary
notes: The signed chain \(\{x\cdot\xi>0\}-\{x\cdot\xi<0\}\) on \(A_{\mathbb R}\) defines \(\alpha_x\in H_{n-1}(A,A_x)\), with \(\partial\alpha_x=2\beta_x\).
statement: In the same oriented even-parity setting, let \(f_x\) denote the real function induced by the linear form after trivializing the real hyperplane line bundle over \(A_{\mathbb R}\). The signed fundamental chain \(\operatorname{sgn}(f_x)[A_{\mathbb R}]\) is a relative cycle of \((A,A_x)\), defining \(\alpha_x\in H_{N-2}(A,A_x;\mathbb C)\). With consistent boundary orientation, \(\partial\alpha_x=2\beta_x\), because the two sides contribute with the same boundary sign after the negative side is subtracted.
reconstruction: The sign of a homogeneous linear form is not intrinsically defined on a real projective point without a lift/trivialization. The source supplies exactly this missing choice. \(\alpha\) is relative, not generally an absolute cycle.
fate: The construction and factor two appear in \citet[\S1, pp.~91--92]{atiyah1967hyperbolic}.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026, this remains an established construction under the stated hypotheses.

title: Constancy of Petrovsky classes within a chamber
notes: When \(x\) moves in one connected component of the cone complement, \(\alpha_x\) and \(\beta_x\) do not change; the notation becomes \(\alpha_C,\beta_C\).
statement: Over a component \(C\) of the complement of the dual discriminant, the smooth hyperplane sections and pairs \((A,A_x)\) form locally trivial families. Their homology groups are identified by continuation along paths, under which the geometrically defined classes \(\alpha_x\) and \(\beta_x\) are locally constant. In particular their vanishing is independent of the chosen \(x\in C\). This is a statement in the corresponding homology local systems, not literal equality of elements of different groups without identification.
reconstruction: The local-system interpretation supplies the missing comparison maps; no global choice of an entire homology basis or absence of monodromy is asserted.
fate: Stated before the two criteria in \citet[\S1, p.~92]{atiyah1967hyperbolic}.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026, this remains an established construction under the stated hypotheses.

title: Stable-lacuna criterion below the dimension
notes: If the order \(m\) and the dimension \(n+1\) are even and \(m<n+1\), \(\beta_C=0\) is necessary and sufficient for a stable lacuna.
statement: Let \(N>2\) and \(m\) be even, \(m<N\), and let \(a\) be real homogeneous and strictly hyperbolic with smooth complex characteristic hypersurface. A component \(C\subset\{x_0>0\}\setminus B\) is a stable lacuna in the zero-solution sense if and only if \(\beta_C=0\) in \(H_{N-3}(A_x;\mathbb C)\).
reconstruction: Complex homology coefficients, complex smoothness, strict hyperbolicity, and \(N>2\) are supplied from the report's precise source. An integral-homology torsion obstruction is not part of this theorem.
fate: Petrovsky's theorem, restated in \citet[Theorem~1, p.~92]{atiyah1967hyperbolic}, circulated in the February 1967 lecture before this report.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026, the criterion is established. Atiyah's June 1967 addendum additionally says that in this low-order regime every lacuna is stable; the addendum postdates the seminar. Later broader formulations appear in \citet[\S10]{atiyahbottgarding1970lacunas}.

title: Stable-lacuna criterion at or above the dimension
notes: If \(m\ge n+1\), with \(m,n+1\) even, \(\alpha_C=0\) is necessary and sufficient for a stable lacuna.
statement: Under the same strict-hyperbolicity and smoothness assumptions, let \(N>2\) and \(m\) be even with \(m\ge N\). Then \(C\) is a stable lacuna if and only if \(\alpha_C=0\) in \(H_{N-2}(A,A_x;\mathbb C)\). The necessary condition \(\beta_C=0\), obtained from \(\partial\alpha_C=2\beta_C\), is weaker and cannot replace the relative-class condition in this regime.
reconstruction: The parity, homology field, and regularity are retained from the exact source. This statement addresses stability, not the classification of all accidental lacunas or all singular wavefronts.
fate: The exact statement is \citet[Theorem~2, p.~92]{atiyah1967hyperbolic}, after Petrovsky and before the March report.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026, the criterion is classical. Atiyah's June 1967 addendum excludes nontrivial stable lacunas in this even-dimensional high-order regime; later terminology calls the notebook's zero regions strong lacunas \citep[pp.~185--188]{atiyahbottgarding1970lacunas}.

title: The projective canonical bundle and Euler form
notes: The notes write \(K_{\mathbb{CP}^n}\simeq\mathcal O(-n-1)\), assert a unique holomorphic \(n\)-form with one pole of order \(n+1\), and give \(\omega=\sum(-1)^j x_j\,dx_0\wedge\cdots\widehat{dx_j}\cdots\wedge dx_n\).
statement: With \(N=n+1\), \(K_{\mathbb{CP}^{N-1}}\simeq\mathcal O(-N)\) and \(H^0(K(N))\simeq\mathbb C\), whereas \(H^0(K)=0\). Thus a nonzero generator is unique up to scalar as a twisted canonical section, or as a meromorphic top form with poles of order at most \(N\) along a fixed hyperplane. On the affine cone its homogeneous representative is \[\omega=\sum_{j=0}^{N-1}(-1)^j\xi_j\,d\xi_0\wedge\cdots\wedge\widehat{d\xi_j}\wedge\cdots\wedge d\xi_{N-1}.\]
reconstruction: The coordinates are renamed \(\xi\) to distinguish symbol space from the physical variable. The cone expression has homogeneity \(N\); it is not an ordinary global holomorphic top form on projective space. A fixed polar hyperplane and uniqueness up to scalar replace the literal ``unique holomorphic form with a pole.
fate: The exact twisted-bundle formulation is \citet[\S2, p.~93]{atiyah1967hyperbolic}.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026, this remains an established construction under the stated hypotheses.

title: Poincare residue with the required homogeneity
notes: The residue form is introduced by \(\omega/a=(da/a)\wedge\omega_a+\Theta\). An overwritten parenthesis appears to say that \(\Theta\) is zero on \(a=0\).
statement: For a smooth hypersurface \(A=\{a=0\}\), the local decomposition of a meromorphic top form with a simple pole is \(\omega/a=(da/a)\wedge\eta+\Theta\), where \(\Theta\) is holomorphic and \(\omega_a=\eta|_A\) is the residue. With homogeneous projective representatives, \(\omega_a\) is a section of \(K_A\otimes\mathcal O(N-m)\); since \(K_A\simeq\mathcal O(m-N)\), the twist is essential unless \(m=N\). Multiplying by a homogeneous polynomial of degree \(m-N\), when \(m\ge N\), produces an ordinary holomorphic top form on \(A\).
reconstruction: The pullback of the holomorphic remainder to the hypersurface vanishes by degree; its coefficient functions need not vanish there. The exact overwritten parenthesis is not resolved by this interpretation. Local residues glue with the displayed twist, rather than as an untwisted form in every degree.
fate: The residue and line-bundle twists are explicit in \citet[\S2, p.~93]{atiyah1967hyperbolic}.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026, this remains an established construction under the stated hypotheses.

title: The Herglotz–Petrovsky residue integral
notes: For \(m\ge n+1\) the final formula is \(E(x)=c\int_{A_{\mathbb R}}\operatorname{sgn}(x\cdot\xi)(x\cdot\xi)^{m-n-1}\omega_a\), followed by a reference to the first volume of generalized functions.
statement: Under the smooth, strictly hyperbolic setting above, with \(m,N\) even and \(m\ge N>2\), the analytic value of the retarded fundamental solution for \(x_0>0\), away from the dual discriminant, is \[E(x)=c_{m,N}\int_{A_{\mathbb R}}\operatorname{sgn}(f_x)\,(x\cdot\xi)^{m-N}\omega_a.\] Orientations and the real line-bundle trivialization are those used for \(\alpha_x\). The polynomial factor cancels the projective twist of the residue; the normalization constant depends on the Fourier convention, the chosen generator, and the normalization of \(P\). The fundamental solution is understood distributionally on the wavefront.
reconstruction: The parity and dimension restrictions are inherited from the theorem, not repeated in the final notebook line. The shorthand constant is not assigned an unsupported numerical value. The formula supplies the announced proof route, but the omitted converse uses substantial algebraic geometry and is not proved in these pages.
fate: The exact formula is \citet[\S2, equation (2.1), p.~93]{atiyah1967hyperbolic}; its classical origin is described in \citet[Chapter~III]{petrovsky1945lacunas}.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026, this residue representation is established. Generalized formulas and their conventions are developed in \citet[\S7]{atiyahbottgarding1970lacunas}.
